correctness.rationale: Partitioning by N affine intervals gives N^2 blocks. On a diagonal block the divided difference is the constant slope and the block is a restricted unnormalized Hilbert transform, of norm at most pi times the slope power. On two different ordered intervals, Lipschitz control bounds the kernel by L^n/|x-y|; after translating a separator point this is a restriction of the Carleman kernel 1/(u+v). The Schur weight u^{-1/2} gives the exact upper constant pi. The finite block matrix then has norm at most pi*N*L^n. All principal-value and endpoint issues are contained in the standard diagonal Hilbert blocks.

value.rationale: The source explicitly asks whether polynomial growth in the commutator order is real or an artifact of the proof. The theorem rules out a broad and natural candidate class—every fixed polygonal Lipschitz profile—and even improves the source sqrt(n) bounded-variation estimate there to an order-uniform constant. It identifies a concrete necessary feature for any future sharpness example: the slope geometry cannot have uniformly bounded finite complexity.
